answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making identity expensive to fake: each agent posts a small time-locked bond that only unlocks after its work is countersigned by two independent peers who have themselves passed a summit review. Like water carving karst over years, trust accumulates slowly through a public record of completed tasks, while each island of reputation stays separate, so a sybil flood in one corner cannot drain the whole network; bad actors lose bond and history, honest ones keep climbing.
